Cube004_1.title: Classification model performance monitoring and forecast

panel.hook: Estimating model performance in production — without ever seeing the ground truth.

description.heading: Project Brief
description.content: A production-oriented monitoring system that estimates classification model performance when true labels aren't available, combining confidence-based metrics with drift detection to catch silent model degradation early.

overview.heading: What It Does
items: Estimates classification performance without ground truth labels using NannyML's CBPE methods
Combines confidence-based metrics with univariate and multivariate drift detection to detect early signs of model degradation
Enables early detection and explanation of performance degradation
Validated across four datasets, including a simulated credit-scoring environment

howItWorks.heading: Under the Hood
howItWorks.content: The system tracks shifts in input feature distributions (univariate and multivariate drift) alongside model confidence signals, correlating both against known degradation patterns to flag when a live model's real-world accuracy is likely slipping.

Cube013_1.title: Scientific Research — Indri Behavioral & Tourism Analysis

panel.hook: Co-author and data analyst investigating how tourism conditions influence Indri behavior and habitat use in Madagascar.

description.heading: Research Brief
description.content: The research combines structured field observations with quantitative statistical analysis. The first study analyzed 816 scan samples and 359 foraging observations from six Indri groups using statistical test to compare foraging support characteristics across tourism-exposure groups. The second study analyzed 220 tourist–Indri encounters to examine how tourist behavior and group size were associated with Indri responses.

overview.heading: Research Contributions
items: Analyzed observational data on Indri habitat use, foraging behavior, tourist interactions, and group size
Applied statistical methods to identify differences in foraging support height and tree diameter across tourism-exposure groups
Produced data visualizations and statistical interpretations supporting the research findings
Contributed to research published in Human-Animal Interactions and American Journal of Primatology
